guardianfootball.title: Raya injured but Madueke rescues point for Arsenal in seesaw Newcastle draw
guardianfootball.description: If Mikel Arteta was delighted to see the back of Eddie Howe as Newcastle’s head coach, the bad news is that another similarly awkward technical area adversary has been installed at St James’ Park. Arsenal’s manager never seemed to relish trips to face Howe’s old team and he certainly did not enjoy this latest trip to Tyneside, where Matthias Jaissle’s initially overwhelmed team fought back commendably to earn a point courtesy of a stellar second-half performance. At half-time the crowd had felt close to turning against Jaissle but he held his nerve and, thanks to a triple substitution and subtle tactical rejig suggested he is no mug after all. Continue reading...

guardianfootball.title: ‘Fragile’ Chelsea must toughen up after Leeds humiliation, admits Xabi Alonso
guardianfootball.description: Xabi Alonso is straying towards crisis territory. Here’s a mind-bending statistic: Chelsea are eighth but have now lost more league games than Manchester United. They were bullied by a rampant Leeds United, who fully merited their first win at Stamford Bridge since going top with a 2-0 victory in December 1999, and can look forward to another season with no European football if they do not sharpen up soon. It is not really worth dwelling on the fact that the second Leeds goal, a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty converted early in an astonishingly one-sided second half, came after Morgan Rogers was harshly penalised for handball. That was a minor detail given the wider picture. Leeds, superbly…

guardianfootball.title: Coventry edge thriller to keep Crystal Palace bottom and ruin Thomas Frank’s start
guardianfootball.description: New manager, new formation, familiar defensive failings. Twice Crystal Palace equalised. They seemed to have stabilised after half-time. But sometimes the rot is so deep-rooted that the new manager bounce manifests as nothing more than it not looking quite as shambolic as it did before. Thomas Frank started with a defeat that means Palace remain bottom of the table having lost five league games in a row. Yet for much of the second half, there had been reasons for Palace optimism. They seemed to have settled better after a ludicrous first half in which neither side looked at all capable of defending. But a triple substitution by Frank Lampard with 20 minutes to go shifted the game back in…

guardianfootball.title: Aston Villa held at home as dogged Sunderland battle for Régis Le Bris
guardianfootball.description: For Aston Villa , a painful stalemate at home to Sunderland, but for Régis Le Bris and his players, this was another triumph of sorts. The raw numbers spoke volumes of Villa’s struggles against a defence that backed themselves to keep Unai Emery’s side at bay. All but one of Villa’s seven shots on target came from outside the visitors’ box and the one inside it, courtesy of Ian Maatsen, was forgettable. Owing to a summer of change, injuries and Emery resting John McGinn with Tuesday’s game at Galatasaray in mind, Maatsen, incredibly, was the sole survivor in the Villa starting XI from when these sides played out a 4-3 classic seven months ago. Villa were too predictable, short of a spark,…

guardianfootball.title: Pochettino needs New Manager Bounce to break torrid Manchester United turnover | Jonathan Wilson
guardianfootball.description: Latest hire will depend on fresh faces and time to bed in at Old Trafford where the dugout churn is hardest to budge Everybody knows the pattern. Performances fade. Results falter. A title challenge becomes clinging on for the last Champions League spot becomes mid-table. Or a promising start becomes a troubling dip, becomes a full-on battle against relegation. Fans begin to grumble. The media wonder whether the spark has gone. Players look disaffected. A dressing room, once lost, is seldom rediscovered, and few managers are given the opportunity to find it again. A crisis in football, once acknowledged, is only ever resolved in one way: by the sacking of the manager. Continue reading...

After hard-fought 1-0 wins against Manchester City last Saturday and Paris Saint-Germain on Wednesday night , Chelsea drew a blank. Against Gareth Taylor’s side, Chelsea’s lack of cutting edge was clear a week after they beat City to go top. The calf injury picked up by Melvine Malard against City, the absence of Lauren James, who has a thigh injury, and the…

Sabah Kerjota and Pierre Landry Kaboré both scored twice with Claudio Braga, Sabri Guendouz, Stuart Findlay and a Ryan Finnigan own goal completing the rout. Vrancken was naturally delighted that his players had ended a run of three defeats in a row in such spectacular style. Continue reading...

Doué went down after twisting awkwardly late in the first half as he tried to control the ball, shortly after scoring to put PSG 2-1 ahead. The match was stopped for five minutes to allow Doué to receive treatment to his right knee before he was carried off to a backdrop of applause from the crowd at the Allianz Riviera stadium. This, as it turns out, is not the statement vehicle it is in London but a practical truck with room for a pallet of fish in the back. When I hop in, Graham, who is...

quietus.description: Kat Lister looks at a radical shift in the 'open road' narrative as exemplified in Joni Mitchell's relatively overlooked eighth album In October of this year, a 17-person expedition voyaged 2,500 miles from the coastline of Papua New Guinea, to a remote Pacific lagoon, looking for Amelia Earhart’s lost aircraft. Satellite images some six years earlier had shown what was believed to be a submerged object with a metallic glint in shallow water. And the glint suggested something to the expedition’s leader, Richard Pettigrew, even if that “something” turned out to be illusory. Which it did. "You know, Amelia herself said, 'Adventure is worthwhile in itself',” he mused with reporters upon his…

The full-length concert recording includes 27 songs arranged in 2 sets, and was captured during the group's November 2024 concerts at the Sydney Opera House. It will be made available in a triple-vinyl edition, as well as in a crystal-clear triple-vinyl limited edition version. The new live album follows on from the 2021 release of The Comeback Special – Live At The Royal Albert Hall.…

quietus.description: Clapton Hymns, Vol. 1 collects 12 live performance recordings captured at the London event series Photo by Joe Hart Church Of Sounds has launched a record label, and its first release is a compilation made up of live performance recordings captured at the London event series. Taking in 12 tracks, Clapton Hymns, Vol. 1 features recordings by Tortoise's Jeff Parker, Moses Boyd's Exodus and Collocutor, among others. Perhaps the standout, though, is a performance by Tony Allen of 'Never (Lagos Never Gonna Be The Same)', which was captured during the legendary Nigerian artist's final live show just 48 days before his death. Church Of Sound was founded in 2016 by Lex Blondin and Spencer Martin.…

Even friends who weren’t necessarily into electronica were taken by its surreal cover, its psychedelic wanderings. The haunting synth melodies, processed vocal samples and polite beats felt like the soundtrack to a lost 1970’s science and nature TV program. Dazed and enthralled, I scoured record stores, looking high and low for anything more from this band. Who were they? Did they land on Earth, release one album and then return to…

With Chicago's Yr Knives, he adds yet another group to the mix. On the group's debut, Begin Yr Singing , he joins drummer Quin Kirchner and guitarists Brian J Sulpizio (Health & Beauty) and Andrew Trim for a wild ride that hypnotically blends progressive rock, free jazz, krautrock, and desert blues. If one were scrambling for a genre, you could select "post-rock," but could equally apply the even less loved term "jazz…

aquariumdrunkard.title: Trio Ternura :: A Gira / Razão De Ser
aquariumdrunkard.description: Trio Ternura—the Brazilian sibling group consisting of sisters Jussara and Jurema and brother Robson Ternura—has been receiving the reissue treatment via Madrid’s Vampisoul label since last year and we are absolutely here for it. Last year, they dished out a new pressing of the group’s 1973 single “A Gira” b/w “Last Tango in Paris.” The A-side is a polyrhythmic groove with tribal percussion and silky, chanting harmonies which finds itself paired with a glittery lounge rendering of Argentinean saxophonist Gato Barbieri’s Grammy-winning film score.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Transmissions :: Larry Crane (Tape Op)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Today on Transmissions, a conversation with Larry Crane of Tape Op magazine. This year, Larry and Tape Op celebrated 30 years of creative advice with Making Music , a book that collects 26 of the best ever interviews from the magazine, including creators like Glyn Johns, Tony Visconti, RZA, Brian Eno, Joe Boyd, Lee “Scratch” Perry, and many more. It’s not just for recording aficionados, but it never skimps on glorious detail.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Sterlin Harjo :: The Aquarium Drunkard Interview
aquariumdrunkard.description: FX’s The Lowdown , which stars Ethan Hawke as an investigative journalist and self-professed "truthstorian," isn’t trying to hide anything from studio executives or its audience. The Lowdown is a hilarious, lovingly shambolic, shaggy dog crime show. It’s dazzling and comprehensive musical selection is led by the show’s creator/executive producer/writer/director Sterlin Harjo. The filmmaker—who is Seminole/Muscogee, grew up in Oklahoma, and currently lives in Tulsa—joins us to discuss the show's unique sound.

aquariumdrunkard.title: Inspiration, Not Limitation :: The Residents’ Eskimo Journey
aquariumdrunkard.description: Many people have seen the Residents, but few know what their members actually look like. The group has maintained anonymity for over 50 years, through hundreds of releases, concerts, books, films, and pretty much every other kind of media. Still, if you've heard of them, you probably know their signature look: tuxedo with top hat perched upon a helmet that resembles a big, veiny eyeball. But did you know the eyeball wasn't always part of the Residents story?

aquariumdrunkard.title: Ben Webster :: Music For Loving (1955)
aquariumdrunkard.description: Music for Loving (1955) contains some of Ben Webster’s most sophisticated and elegant work, and the larger arrangements avoid the pitfalls of the “jazz-with-strings” genre. This is none more apparent than when the orchestral bells and whistles step aside, allowing Webster and his band the space to linger in the crestfallen ballads.

mubi.title: The Last Emperor: A Conversation with Jeremy Thomas
mubi.description: The Last Emperor (Bernardo Bertolucci, 1987). When Jeremy Thomas died on September 11, 2026, the British film industry lost a titan. A producer who paid no heed to the vagaries of popular culture, Thomas was led by his impeccable palate for cinematic ambition, unswayed by whether audiences or critics came along for the ride. A list of filmmakers whose work makes up Thomas’s production portfolio reads like a who’s who of maverick visionaries, each of them fiercely loyal to the last: Nicolas Roeg and David Cronenberg; Takeshi Kitano and Jonathan Glazer; Nagisa Ōshima and Wim Wenders; Jerzy Skolimowski and Bernardo Bertolucci, whose The Last Emperor (1987) won Thomas the Academy Award for…
